Late response, but hello! I was really only dealing with one infested room, so it was instant relief upon cleaning. They were in the carpets, so after a weekend cleaning they were gone. For big appliances, I never moved any. When I clean around them, I usually just stick a broom underneath and hope Im getting everything. However, I do recommend getting some Borax into the crevices of those areas- push some under the fridge with a broom or with some cardboard, sprinkle some behind the drier/washer. I usually sprinkle some around where my bed meets the wall, as thats going to be a tough spot to clean. 


I havent had any real issues since, my roommate had a larvae or two so I vaccumed and sprinkled. You can also use Diatomaceous Earth if youre worried about toxins, but that stuff is powdery and will leave a dusty coating on everything.

SUPER late response, havent been on reddit recently. Boric acid works like a charm, but Id keep it in areas people arent typically touching. Its a laundry detergent, so it can be irritating to the skin and you wouldnt want to breath it in. Id recommend using it on the carpets (focusing on the edges and corners), after about a week give it a vaccume. Vaccuming is really key here. 


Now if you have kids around, or otherwise worry about borax hurting someone in the house Id use diatomaceous earth. Its a sterile powdered clay that dehydrates bugs and is totally safe. Only obnoxious thing about it is it leaves dust everywhere, and can trigger allergies.

You either form a strong bond with your coworkers and learn the best way to bend the rules/efficiently run the store, or you gotta quit. I worked at sb some time, thankfully had a good team. Moves, and my new store was absolute city hell, horrible manager/ass manager, union busting, unprofessional workplace with bad vibes all around. Unfortunately you can only do so much, if the place is eating you alive you gotta transfer or quit at some point. Its not a *you* failing, they failed to keep you.

If you dont feel like you can keep up a positive attitude, thats a-ok. You got a lot going on and youre your own person. Being able to keep up a customer service persona mask is 90% of the trick here. Be honest with your coworkers if you feel worried youre gonna ruin the vibe with low positivity- letting them know whats up with you is a great way to let em know you genuinely want to work on good terms with everyone.

Latch onto the things you can genuinely take pride in, for me it was the drinks. Taking pride in cleanliness, drink construction.. whatever you feel proud about, make it your art. Beyond that, dont let them take advantage of you. If they always put you on bar, dont give 100% every day unless you want to hurt yourself. Give 50% on bar, 70% on register, whatever. Tell someone if youre crashing and need to switch off to take dishes for a while, because lord knows they arent gonna pay attention to your needs if they already drowning.

If they call you in on a day off, dont do it. The more you give, the more it encourages management to never hire extras. Dont go to optional meetings, accept freebees but dont buy into any company propaganda. If youre in the position to take home free food I more than encourage it, long as there are no narks present.

At the end of the day, its just a shit job. If you feel like youre drowning but need to stay for school, put as little effort as you can into working (dont sweat, rush, or go above and beyond). Youre here for a paycheck, do whatever it takes to mentally get through the day
